To demonstrate the bug, let's say I run (using starlette `v0.13.2`): ```py from pathlib import Path from starlette.applications import Starlette from starlette.middleware import Middleware from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware from starlette.responses import Response from starlette.routing import Route from starlette.templating import Jinja2Templates from starlette.testclient import TestClient p = Path('templates') p.mkdir(exist_ok=True) (p / 'index.html').write_text('

1 + 1 = {{ 1 + 1 }}

\n') templates = Jinja2Templates(directory=p) async def view(request): # return Response('raw response') # this works fine return templates.TemplateResponse('index.html', {'request': request}) class CustomHeaderMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware): async def dispatch(self, request, call_next): response = await call_next(request) response.headers['Custom'] = 'Example' return response app = Starlette( debug=True, middleware=[Middleware(CustomHeaderMiddleware)], routes=[Route('/', view)], ) def test_app(): client = TestClient(app) response = client.get('/') assert response.status_code == 200 print(f'response text: {response.text!r}') print(f'"Custom" header: {response.headers.get("Custom")!r}') if __name__ == '__main__': print('running tests...') test_app() print('tests passed') ``` I get the exception: ``` File ".../env/lib/python3.8/site-packages/starlette/middleware/base.py", line 47, in call_next assert message["type"] == "http.response.start" ```
